objective_for_doctor:
Age: 58
Sex: Female
Chief Complaint: I have episodes of suffocation, trouble keeping your tongue in your mouth, and a hard time opening/raising one or both eyelids

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: Hi. I’ve been having episodes where it feels like I can’t breathe—like I’m suffocating—and I also have trouble keeping my tongue in my mouth. My face and neck have annoying muscle spasms, and my neck feels sore so I can’t turn my head to one side, and sometimes I have trouble opening or raising one or both eyelids. I also have jaw difficulty, like it’s hard to open my mouth.

turns.doctor_question: I’m sorry you’re dealing with this. Do you have any pain somewhere in your body that’s related to why you’re consulting today? (Yes/No)
turns.patient_answer: No, I don’t have pain right now—my pain is 0 out of 10.

turns.doctor_question: Do you have a cough right now? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: No, I don’t have a cough right now.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been treated in a hospital recently for nausea, agitation, intoxication, or aggressive behavior, and received medication through an IV (intravenous) or a shot (intramuscular)?
turns.patient_answer: Yes. I was treated in the hospital recently for nausea and agitation/intoxication-type issues, and I received medication through an IV or a shot.

turns.doctor_question: In the past 7 days, have you started taking—or taken any antipsychotic medication (for example, medicines like risperidone, quetiapine, olanzapine, aripiprazole, or haloperidol)?
turns.patient_answer: I’m not sure about the exact names, but yes—I was given medications in the hospital, and I think some of them may have been antipsychotic-type. I can’t confidently list which ones.

turns.doctor_question: Do you regularly take stimulant drugs (for example, medications like ADHD stimulants or other stimulants)?
turns.patient_answer: No, I don’t regularly take stimulant drugs.

turns.doctor_question: Are you unable to control the direction of your eyes (for example, they won’t move where you want them to)?
turns.patient_answer: I don’t know about eye direction specifically. But I do have trouble opening or raising one or both eyelids during these episodes.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever felt like you were suffocating for a very short time, with an inability to breathe or speak?
turns.patient_answer: Yes. The episodes are like that—very short times where it feels like I can’t breathe, and sometimes I can’t speak normally either.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel your heart beating fast (racing), irregularly (like it’s missing a beat), or palpitations right now?
turns.patient_answer: No, I don’t feel my heart racing or irregular right now.
